newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares jump to new trading high.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares jump to new trading high.

text.p: Istanbul shares further extended earlier strong gains in continued hectic buying at the start of the afternoon trade on Monday amid new government hopes, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 soared 6.94 percent to a new trading record of 1,756 at 1130 GMT in the first half of the afternoon session, compared to a previous record of 1,751 on January 27.
Trade volume stood at around eight trillion lira in the first half hour of the second session, compared to 21.59 trillion in the whole of the first session.
Brokers said the market was buoyed by hopes that Prime Minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz would set up an Islamist-free coalition government.
"The market was very pleased with the appointment of Yilmaz. This rise may continue for a few more days. There has also been strong liquidity inflow," said Cem Baycan from Delta securities.
"There may be some profit-taking but the rise may continue unless a negative expectation emerges ahead of the confidence vote," he added.

Turkish President Suleyman Demirel nominated Yilmaz on Friday to put together a government after the resignation of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, who stays on as caretaker for the time being.

Yilmaz began a meeting of his conservative Motherland Party to plan strategy for his bid to forge an anti-Islamist coalition. The party is discussing ways to woo fellow conservatives from Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's True Path Party into the planned secularist alliance.
Yilmaz is around a dozen votes short of the simple majority of votes needed in parliament to win a confidence vote in a new government.
